issue.title: middleware: TestDocsExample red under load (strategies.fewest-tokens: took too long)
issue.body:
`internal/middleware`'s TestDocsExample went red in a full `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 45m ./...` run on macOS (load average ~140) at bf931f82c plus the uncommitted #2671 change (provider found groups; nothing in middleware or routes):

```
2026/10/17 18:44:51 middleware .../TestDocsExample2088259992/001/spread.gateway.js [error]: strategies.fewest-tokens: took too long
--- FAIL: TestDocsExample (0.04s)
    points_test.go:348: [0 1 2 3] {[] []  0 0 1 strategies.fewest-tokens: took too long [spread/fewest-tokens] 1 true 0 0}
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/middleware	24.227s
```

Run alone right after on the same tree, it passes (3.2s).

The strategy call runs under the middleware's wall-clock budget (`requestLimit` 250ms / `eventLimit` 50ms in middleware.go, `in.rt.Interrupt(errTimeout)`). On a busy machine the docs example's `fewest-tokens` order went past it, so `routes.Apply` fell back to the input order `[0 1 2 3]`.

What the test is about is the example's order. The budget is a separate guarantee, and it is also what a user's strategy meets on a busy machine. The test should either hold the budget out of its way or measure CPU, not wall time. Filed so it isn't left as "passes alone"; not worked on here.

comments.body:
Fixed on [fix/2728-docs-strategy-test-budget](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2728-docs-strategy-test-budget), commit [c01aa5a1](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/c01aa5a10e8771b0f9e89c7c17d8e340581c42b0), based on upstream `ed0ab567`.

`TestDocsExample` now temporarily holds its strategy budget out of the ordering assertion and restores it afterwards. The current production strategy budget is 20 ms; production behavior is unchanged, and the separate fail-open test still verifies that a spinning strategy times out.

The original load-dependent failure was not naturally reproduced. With a deliberately exhausted budget and temporary synchronization on the timer interrupt, the old test fails with identity ordering and the adjusted test passes. Reversing the real JS ordering or making it throw still makes the ordering test fail. Related middleware tests pass under `-race`, including the independent timeout test; scoped middleware/routes vet and build pass. I independently reran the related race tests.

The full suite, full application build and cross-platform runtime were not run. AI-assisted implementation and review.

For whoever picks this up: the branch on #5965 gives every middleware test room past the limits from the package's TestMain (the limit tests set their own), which covers TestDocsExample too; with #3673's 25ms after each arm it goes red without that line and passes with it. skygunner's c01aa5a1 here does the same for TestDocsExample alone, so only one of the two is needed.

issue.title: tests: in-process fakes get production's 20ms to 3s deadlines, and a busy test binary can miss them

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Some tests point production code at a fake that runs inside the test binary (an httptest server, or a JS module run by moejs) and leave the production deadline in front of it. The deadlines are 20ms to 3s, which is right for the real app or module, but the fake gets scheduled along with everything else in the test binary. When the binary stalls a little past the deadline on a busy machine, the code decides the fake isn't there (or is stuck) and the test goes red. #2687 (TestOnUsageRows) and #2728 (TestDocsExample) are two of these that went red under load, and #3639 is the omarchy one.

I put a sleep just past each deadline into each fake, one at a time, on origin/main c158b043 (linux, go1.26.8). For the JS modules it has to go in production code next to the timer, since the module runs on the calling goroutine. Each of these goes red with its sleep and passes without it:

| deadline | fake | tests | sleep | red |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `almaClient` 1.5s, internal/agent/alma.go:54 | `startAlma`, alma_test.go:134 | TestAlma, TestAlmaKey | 1.6s at the top of `fakeAlma.ServeHTTP` (:39) | `alma_test.go:190: get: ""`, `alma_test.go:608: provider after Sync: ...` |
| `hanakoProbe` 1.5s, hanako.go:56 (used at :512) | `fakeHanako`, hanako_test.go:314 | TestHanakoLive, TestHanakoSealed, TestHanakoLiveBackNeedsProviderID | 1.6s at the top of its handler | `puts: []`, and Sealed's `... open OpenHanako and try again` |
| `realReachProbe`'s 2s, reach.go:39 | the test's own httptest | TestReachProbe | 2.1s in its handler | `a 401 taken for nothing listening` |
| `realMagpieProbe`'s 3s, reach.go:54 | httptest around `gateway.New().Handler()` | TestMagpieProbe | 3.1s in its handler | `.../magpie: false, want true` |
| `statuslineWait` 1s, internal/cli/statusline_cli.go:42 | `statuslineGateway`, statusline_cli_test.go:32 | TestStatuslineTellsRouteAndEveryAccount | 1.1s in its quotas handler | `statusline = ""` |
| `strategyLimit` 20ms, internal/middleware/points.go:48 | the test's module | TestStrategiesServedWhileOn, TestOnUsageRows, TestPointsHaveNoNetwork, TestDocsExample | 25ms in `inst.call` right after `in.arm(limit)`, middleware.go:287 | `reverse: [0 1 2]`, `strategies.seen: took too long`, `strategies.probe: took too long`, `[0 1 2 3] ... strategies.fewest-tokens: took too long` |
| `loadLimit` and `connectLimit` 1s, internal/agentplug/agentplug.go:119 | the test's agent.js | internal/agent: TestPluggedYAML, TestPluggedJSONUnwire, TestPluggedRefused; internal/library: TestPluginAgentGetsTheLibrary, TestPluginAgentWithoutAPlaceIsRefused, TestPluginAgentMCPFormat | 1.1s in `limit` before `fn()`, agentplug.go:403 | `agent plugin .../pa didn't load: took too long`, then each test misses its agent |

The runs, each with only its own sleep in place and `git checkout -- .` after:

```
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^(TestAlma|TestAlmaKey)$' ./internal/agent
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^(TestHanakoLive|TestHanakoSealed|TestHanakoLiveBackNeedsProviderID)$' ./internal/agent
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^TestReachProbe$' ./internal/agent
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^TestMagpieProbe$' ./internal/agent
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^TestPlugged(YAML|JSONUnwire|Refused)$' ./internal/agent
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^TestPluginAgent' ./internal/library
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v -run '^TestStatuslineTellsRouteAndEveryAccount$' ./internal/cli
go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v ./internal/middleware
```

In middleware the sleep has to come after the arm. Put right after `start` in `order` instead, it hands `call` a negative limit and the strategy races the timer: the four tests passed 12 to 19 times in 20 that way. After the arm it's 20 of 20 red and nothing else in the package goes red. TestDocsExample's red there is #2728's, `[0 1 2 3]` with `strategies.fewest-tokens: took too long`, so the limit #2728 runs into is `strategyLimit` rather than `requestLimit` or `eventLimit`.

Apart from #2687, #2728 and #3639, I haven't seen any of these go red in a real run. They're the same shape, and the sleep stands in for the stall.

What #2687 asks for works for all of these: a test raises the deadline for its own fake and puts it back after. fbfb76149 did that for copilotSecretWait (#1627), giving the lookups that answer 10 minutes, and the patch on #3639 does it for niri. Tests that check the give-up keep the short one. TestStrategyFailsOpen's `for (;;) {}` needs the 20ms, so the raise goes in the tests that want an answer, not in a helper they share. Some can't be raised from their tests yet. `statuslineWait` is a const, and `realReachProbe` and `realMagpieProbe` set their timeout inline. agentplug's two are vars, but the tests that load modules are in internal/agent and internal/library, so they'd need a `...ForTest` knob like provider's `CodexTokenURLForTest`. `almaClient` and `hanakoProbe` are package `*http.Client`s the agent tests can swap, and `strategyLimit` is a var in the package its tests are in.

#2565 looks like the same thing through the middleware's own hook limits (`requestLimit` 250ms, `eventLimit` 50ms, its `loadLimit` 1s) in a gateway test. I didn't put a sleep in for that one.

The list isn't complete. It's what a grep for production timeouts of 3s or less turned up, minus the ones no test waits on and the ones whose tests already raise them or only check a refusal.

issue.title: middleware: a late timeout interrupt can stop the next call on the runtime

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Found while checking internal/middleware for #3727's case. Each runtime there has one timer, reused for every call:

```go
in.timer = time.AfterFunc(time.Hour, func() {
	in.mu.Lock()
	if in.armed {
		in.fired = true
		in.rt.Interrupt(errTimeout)
	}
	in.mu.Unlock()
})
```

`armed` under the lock keeps #3727's case away: a func that gets the lock after disarm finds nothing armed, and an interrupt it gave before disarm is cleared there, so none sticks. But disarm's `in.timer.Stop()` doesn't wait for a func that has begun either, and nothing ties the func to the call it was set for. When a hook ends just as its time runs out, the func can still be on its way to the lock when the next call on that runtime arms. It then finds `armed` true and stops that call, which had its own time left: it reads "took too long" and its input goes on as it was. That call's disarm clears it, so it's one call, not every one after.

Which call that is depends on what runs next on the runtime: the next event's onEvent in a stream, often microseconds later, so that event reaches the agent as it was (a middleware that masks text lets that one through); another request's onRequest, onProvider or onResponse, since runtimes are pooled; or a strategy or onUsage, which share a runtime the same way. A module load that ends as its second runs out can leave one for the first hook too.

Reproduced at 1bb8143b with a 100ms pause put into the timer's func before it takes the lock, an onRequest that busy-waits 100ms, and requestLimit at 50ms for one request:

```
request before (250ms limit, 100ms of work): changed by its onRequest
request whose timer fires as it finishes (50ms limit, 100ms of work): changed by its onRequest
request after (250ms limit, 100ms of work): kept as it was, onRequest: took too long
request after that (250ms limit, 100ms of work): changed by its onRequest
```

When the pause ends while nothing is armed (the next request 200ms later), the requests after all go through, so it's the next arm that catches it. Without the pause it needs the func to run late by more than the gap to the next call, so it's rare: a hook that takes about its limit, on a busy machine. From outside it reads like #2565, #2687 and #2728, a hook that took too long, but the call it stops here had time left.

What I have in mind: when Stop says the func has begun, disarm waits for it before clearing, as #3727 does, so no func outlives the call it was set for and a call that ends in time pays nothing more. I'll take this one.

issue.title: middleware: TestRequestChain red under load (the first onRequest took too long)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Two internal/middleware tests went red in one full run, both with the module's call ending at its deadline (`took too long`):

```
2026/11/10 21:18:12 middleware /tmp/TestRequestChain170834190/001 [error]: onRequest: took too long
--- FAIL: TestRequestChain (0.66s)
    middleware_test.go:99: body {"model":"m1!"}
--- FAIL: TestStream (0.50s)
    middleware_test.go:338: got
        "event: message_start
data: {"type":"message_start"}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"secret here"}}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"more"}}

data: [DONE]

"
        want
        "event: message_start
data: {"type":"message_start"}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"****** here"}}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"more"}}

data: [DONE]

"
```

`TestRequestChain`: the first module's `onRequest` was cut off at its deadline, so the body is `m1!`, not `m2!`. `TestStream`: the masking `onEvent` didn't run on the first delta, so "secret" went through. Same class as #3673 (in-process fakes get production's 20ms-3s deadlines), #2687 and #2728. Filed per test as the lessons ask; the fix is the class: tests get a deadline with room on a loaded box.

Seen in a full `go test -count=1 -timeout 45m -tags nogui ./...` at 6b92824ff (v0.1.3567) on the Linux box (WSL2 magpie-desktop), under ~/suite.lock but beside another session's unlocked `go test ./internal/claudetui/ ./internal/gateway/` on the same box, so the box was loaded. Log: magpie-wt/norethsea-scratch/suite.log. Not rerun alone; not reproduced with an injected delay.

issue.title: gateway: TestMiddlewareThroughGateway red once: the reply's first text delta skipped the middleware's onEvent

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`internal/gateway` `TestMiddlewareThroughGateway` went red once in `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 45m ./internal/library ./internal/gateway ./internal/gui` on the WSL box (`magpie-desktop`, through wsl-run). The tree was a branch based on 40ca0c88d whose gateway change only adds `HubAgentOf` for the MCP hub's agent names; middleware, redaction and streaming are untouched. The gateway package took 1887s, run beside the library and gui packages.

```
--- FAIL: TestMiddlewareThroughGateway (3.97s)
    middleware_test.go:94: text "hello \"KEY SK-PROJ-ABCDEFGH1234IJKLMNOP5678QRST\"[anthropic]", want "HELLO [anthropic]\"KEY SK-PROJ-ABCDEFGH1234IJKLMNOP5678QRST\"[anthropic]"
```

The first text delta ("hello ") reached the agent without the middleware's `onEvent`, and the second went through it. So within one reply, an event got past the middleware. That looks like a race in when `onEvent` is attached (or in `middleware.Reload()` finishing) and not like load in the test. A user's middleware could miss the start of a reply the same way.

Alone it passes 5 of 5 (`-count=5 -run '^TestMiddlewareThroughGateway$'`, same tree). The cause hasn't been looked for.
